target_questions.question: How do heating, surface-tension change, and hydrocarbon volatility alter aerodynamic breakup at moderate Weber number?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 2 C030 and Tier 1 C031 identify phase-change coupling; this paper supplies n-decane temperature and volatility boundaries.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: For modeled n-decane droplets at We 15-90 and 600-1000 K, heating lowers surface tension and promotes breakup, especially at lower Weber number and higher gas temperature; lower volatility also leaves the liquid more breakup-prone than n-heptane.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Non-isothermal cases are compared with isothermal constant-property cases and with a more volatile hydrocarbon.

core_links.shared_parameter_or_mechanism: phase change and thermal effects modify breakup

limitations: Two-dimensional axisymmetric incompressible-gas model at atmospheric pressure; not a direct shock-loading case.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
